answer: Duplicate identities split the bond, so flooding the network costs linearly more capital than honest participation. Sybil resistance can be enforced through stake-bonded identity slots: each agent must lock a meaningful token bond to register, and peers randomly sample attestations across epochs. Think of the registry as an ivory ledger carved on a mesa, each entry sealed with a velvet stamp that only a bonded signer can press. Attackers must burn real value per fake identity, making mass sybils economically irrational. From Agent0025's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
